newsitem.title: RUSSIA: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SET SIGHTS ON WORLD CUP SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA SET SIGHTS ON WORLD CUP SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Russia said on Wednesday they were aiming for at least a semifinal place at the ice hockey World Cup but their success depended on how many of their foreign-based players would be available.
"The aim is to be among the four best teams at the championship and this may well be achieved," Mikhail Govorkov, spokesman for Russia's ice hockey federation, said.

"But it will depend on how well we manage to bring players together and how we manage to reinforce the team with Russians playing in the National Hockey League (of North America) and in European clubs."

The Soviet Union once dominated ice hockey but Russia have rarely tasted glory since the Soviet empire collapsed in 1991 and many of their top players have gone abroad. Russia last won a world championship in 1993, under coach Boris Mikhailov.

The squad started training in the suburbs of Moscow last week but the line-up is far from complete because coaches are anxiously awaiting the foreign-based players for the tournament in Finland starting on April 26.
Chief coach Igor Dmitriyev said last week he expected some NHL players to join the squad just days before the tournament. Govorkov suggested some might arrive even later.
"Dmitriyev's plan is to have about three places in the squad reserved for NHL reinforcements even after the championship starts," he said.
Vancouver Canucks' "Russian Rocket" Pavel Bure said he wanted to represent Russia but wanted to prove his fitness with the Canucks first after a back injury.
Alexander Mogilny, who also plays for the Canucks, has ruled himself out completely because he wants to be with his wife who is about to give birth.

Govorkov said Russia was negotiating with Ottawa Senators' forward Alexei Yashin, Toronto Maple Leafs' rookie Segei Berezin, former Whaler Andrei Nikolishin of Washington Capitals, Edmonton's Andrei Kovalenko and Andrei Nazarov of San Jose Sharks.

Govorkov said the players already training formed a good nucleus and that Alexei Gorshkov and Dmitry Krasotkin were likely to join the squad from Torpedo Yaroslavl when the Russian championship ended.

Torpedo, undefeated in eight play-off games so far, look well positioned to win the Russian ice hockey crown from Lada Togliatti. Lada, known for their collective game rather than their individuals, are unlikely to provide any squad players.

Other Russian players will be Sergei Fokin and Sergei Bautin who play in Sweden, Dmitry Yerofeyev and Alexander Prokopyev of Czech team Vitkowitse, Anatoly Fedotov and Alexander Barkov of Finland's Tappara and Alexander Kharitonov of Dynamo Moscow.
